_comment: The stamped LINKED tier: how many matched translation units actually reach the
PC port's binary. This is a STAMP, not a live counter, and it cannot be anything
else from main: port/tools/linkage.py reads build/port/walk_window.map, which only
exists after an MSVC build of the port, and CI on main has no such build.
BEFORE STAMPING, LOOK FOR A BUILD THAT ALREADY EXISTS. Every port lane carries its
own build tree, so a current walk_window.map is usually already on disk:
ls -la */build/port/walk_window.map
across the port worktrees, newest first, then run the tool against that root. The
first version of this file was stamped off a five-day-old branch while a map from
the night before sat unread one directory away, and published 26.5% when the real
figure was 34.5%. A stale stamp is still a real measurement, just of the wrong run.
To refresh: run `python port/tools/linkage.py [root]` and update the numbers below
together with branch, commit and measuredAt. Never move the count without also
moving the provenance fields - tools/tiers.py drops a stamp missing any of them,
which is the intended behaviour for a number nobody can trace.
basis records what the figure is a measurement OF. The port branches are not merged,
so this is the best single lane rather than a combined total. All seven live lanes,
lk5 3819. Overlapping but not identical seats, so the merged figure is higher and
the published number stays a floor.
This number moves ONE way: seating a new actor class, worth ~8-10 TUs each.
Enrolling free TUs does nothing, because the release build dead-strips whatever the
linked closure never references.
basis: integration branch port/link100 at its pushed tip 4a9b47965, measured against that tip's own battery build walk_window.map (C:/tmp/l3slot5, lane PMFB3's third gate: tree clean, battery ALL GREEN at floor 10083, five proofs green including the opening-cutscene gate), folded by fast-forward because the lane was gated on the integration tip itself, and confirmed by the hosted-runner port-linkage workflow, which counts every push of port/** and the shipping branch on a GitHub Windows machine with no cartridge and has printed the local number for every push today. +28 over the midday stamp of 10058, +53 over the morning stamp of 10033, +965 over the 2026-08-30 stamp of 9121. The shipping branch port-mount-noseat-cluster is fast-forwarded to the same commit. Since the 10058 stamp, all in the pointer-to-member family: the two ov006 sound-state level-1 dispatchers behind a boot installer that checks every slot against the ROM address and a zero adjust word before writing a host address, then the thirteen level-2 sub-dispatchers through the same installer with one-argument __fastcall faces (the matched code calls with the receiver in ecx and the callee cleaning); the Bird and Flag Renders once the ModelAnim table was ROM-ordered; five Behavior dispatchers (PathLift, OneUpMushroom, Coin, PowerStar, PiranhaPlant) and the Enemy death pair on faces sized from each row's own listing; SoundObject::Behavior with the port's out-of-range refusal moved ahead of the matched code (the cartridge's own gate is off by one: parameter 7 runs off two seven-entry tables); and the three table-reading dScMgBase framework dispatchers. Gated rungs since the last stamp: 10058 -> 10069 -> 10086. Remaining: the call-shape rows over tables that have no installing seat yet, six framework rows that read an object field written by four setters, the cutscene trio (two pointers-to-member per slot, filled field by field), the wireless chain behind the ARM7 model (~175), the boot chain's refused arms, and guessed vtable bodies that need real decomp.
